title: Limits of earlier sequence models
text:
Limits of earlier sequence models
• RNN: sequential steps; long-range signal takes many hops
• CNN: parallel but local receptive fields
Need
A layer where every token can read every other token — subject to masks —
and training can parallelize over the sequence axis.

title: What Transformer brings
text:
What Transformer brings
• Direct token–token interaction (attention)
• Parallel training over positions
• One reusable block stacked L times
Causal LMs: training still parallel with a causal mask; generation is sequential at inference
(Lecture 2).

title: Hyperparameters at this level
text:
Hyperparameters at this level
• B: batch size — number of sequences processed together
• n: sequence length — tokens per sequence (often padded)
• d: model width — embedding / hidden size
• L: depth — number of stacked Encoder blocks
• h: heads;
dh = d/h: per-head width
Tensor shape through the stack: (B, n, d).

• One head learns one attention pattern
• Multiple heads can learn different interaction patterns in parallel
Specialization is an intuition — not every head has a clean human-interpretable role.

Y = A @ V

title: Keras sketch (pre-norm)
text:
Keras sketch (pre-norm)
x = LayerNormalization()(inputs)
attn = MultiHeadAttention(num_heads=8, key_dim=64)(x, x)
x = Add()([inputs, attn])
y = Dense(4*d, activation="gelu")(LayerNormalization()(x))
outputs = Add()([x, Dense(d)(y)])
API: key dim maps to our dh (per-head width).
